name: Liberia
headline: Liberia: +5.1% growth in 2025, 8.3% inflation, debt 55% of GDP
sections: Liberia is a $5.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 172nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.1% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $1,981 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K.
Consumer prices rose 8.3% in 2025, above typical targets. Unemployment stood at 2.9% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 2.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 55% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 59% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.1% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −7.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 9.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 51% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 62.3 years (2024). Population: 5.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
